column2: SSE: streaming UTF-8 decode across chunk boundaries

pi TextDecoder strips a leading BOM by default, so "﻿data: {...}" parses. ri from_utf8_lossy keeps the BOM; strip_prefix("data:") fails and the first event is silently dropped. Scenario: server prepends BOM to the SSE body: pi yields the first event, ri loses it.

pi rewrites all

column2: SSE: event dispatch on blank line (split on \n\n)
column5: pi splits buffer on "\n\n"; ri dispatches pending data_lines on each empty line. Same framing; consecutive blank lines are no-ops in both (ri: data_lines empty -> return; pi: empty chunk has no data line).

column2: SSE: "data:" prefix with/without space, whitespace trim
column5: pi slice(5)+trim (both ends, all whitespace); ri strip_prefix("data:")+trim_start (leading only). Trailing whitespace difference is immaterial: serde_json tolerates trailing ws and the [DONE] comparison re-trims. "data:x" (no space) and "data:  x" behave identically in both.
pi: data !== "[DONE]" after trim; ri: data.trim() == "[DONE]" -> return. Same.
pi: empty/absent data is falsy -> no event; ri: no data lines -> return; empty joined data fails parse -> dropped. Same net effect.

column2: SSE: invalid JSON in data frame
column5: pi JSON.parse throws -> the generator throws -> request surfaces a stream error. ri push_sse_event uses `if let Ok(...)` and SILENTLY DROPS unparseable frames, continuing the stream. Scenario: backend emits one corrupted frame "data: {trunc\n\n" mid-stream: pi aborts the response with an error event; ri skips the frame and keeps consuming (may still finish successfully).
ri parses SSE data via parse_json_with_repair (fixes bad escapes, raw control chars, lone surrogate escapes -> �) before giving up; pi uses strict JSON.parse. ri accepts frames pi would reject.

column5: pi regex deletes lone high/low surrogates (paired emoji untouched). ri sanitize_surrogates is an IDENTITY function - sound because Rust &str can never contain unpaired surrogates - but the equivalent inputs take a different path: lone-surrogate JSON escapes are rewritten to � at ingestion by repair_json (json_repair.rs:85,90).
